column15: FlavorText
A weathered blade with a surprisingly keen edge, unearthed from a crumbling waystation deep in bandit territory.
A single-headed axe etched with wind runes that emit a faint whistle when swung with force.
A gnarled staff carved from the heartwood of a petrified treant. The wood still channels residual elemental energy.
A recurve bow fashioned from coldwood harvested in the highland barrens. Its limbs hold tension like a living creature.
A blade of pale grey steel whose edge shimmers like drifting smoke. Sought by shadow hunters. Peerless in swiftness.

column12: A rough-hewn helmet fashioned from hardened bark and cured leather. Offers modest protection for those just starting out.
A lightweight circlet set with a pale grey gemstone that quietly amplifies magical focus. Common among travelling mages.
A fearsome iron mask forged to resemble a snarling beast. Those who don it are said to take on the creature's ferocity.

column1: 29707: Haste reduced from +3 to +2 (Haste+3 on a helm is too strong even at lv60)

column12: A plain white coat bearing faded sigils of a forgotten faith. Worn by wandering healers across many regions.
Battle-worn plate still faintly warm to the touch as though embers smoulder within the steel. Stolen from a fire cultist warlord.
A tunic woven from threads that absorb ambient light. The wearer moves with unnerving silence. Proof of a master assassin.

column1: 29710: Haste reduced from +4 to +3 (still Tier 4 body - kept Triple Attack+1%)

column12: Supple leather mitts reinforced with copper wire that crackles faintly in stormy weather. A scout's favoured tool.
Iron gauntlets engineered to convert raw force into surgical strikes. Built to humble rather than shatter.

column1: 29711: Ranged Accuracy trimmed from +7 to +5; Wind Ele Acc from +5 to +4

column12: Hardy leather legwear designed for those who spend long hours crossing rough terrain. Practical over pretty.
Slacks lined with a faintly humming enchanted weave. The name comes from the forlorn look of the scholar who first wore them.
Lightweight boots with an unusually flexible sole that leaves almost no footprint. A poacher's best kept secret.
Elegant sabots set with dull grey gemstones that pulse when a hex is cast. They sharpen the bite of debilitating magic.

column13: A necklace strung with polished crimson beads. A common talisman among mercenaries who can't afford proper armour.
A waist sash of golden-threaded fabric. Worn as a mark of scholarly achievement in several schools of arcane study.
A well-travelled cape carrying the faint scent of distant lands. Light enough never to slow the wearer down.

column15: FlavorText
A sturdy club fashioned from ironwood root. Favoured by travelling healers who prefer something heavier than a wand.
A slender blade carved to resemble a viper's fang. Traders swear its strike carries a subtle numbing sting.
A broad two-handed axe whose blade is worn to a rough edge from overuse. Hard to argue with the results.
A wickedly curved scythe imbued with faint necrotic energy. Hums audibly in the presence of the recently deceased.
A polearm tipped with a cluster of serrated thorns. Made by a retired drachen soldier with too much time and iron.
Iron-capped knuckle guards that transmit impact with brutal efficiency. Standard equipment in the border monasteries.
A blade of deep blue steel that holds its edge remarkably well. Named for the cobalt ore used in its forging.
A long-barrelled musket built from black ashwood and dark iron. Its report echoes further than most, they say.
A greataxe reinforced with banded bone from a colossal beast. Carries the weight of something that refused to die easily.
A simple recurve bow strung from dried reeds. Makes a whispering sound in flight. Cheap to replace and easy to carry.

column12: A battered leather cap worn by field wardens and game scouts. Smells faintly of wet bark and old sweat.
A stiff academic cap embroidered with old sigils. Uncomfortable to wear but appreciated by those who know what it means.
A dark cloth bandana knotted tight across the brow. A dozen different bandits have been hanged wearing one just like it.
A gilded crown of heavy iron plate bearing the crest of a disbanded holy order. Still inspires pause in those who recognise it.
A featureless visor that conceals the wearer's expression entirely. Unsettling in a melee and worse in a negotiation.
A vest stitched from rough ashgrain cloth. Offers little in the way of prestige but keeps the wearer moving freely.
A robe dyed in deep twilight hues that fade into shadow at the edges. Woven through with faint channelling thread.
A reinforced chainmail hauberk with overlapping iron plates at the shoulders. Trusted by career soldiers everywhere.
A surcoat bearing the seal of a mountain monastery. The cloth is heavy with blessing layered over generations.
A long coat of blackened lamellar plates. The mark of a reaver—someone who has cut a path through stronger opponents.
Thick hide gloves worn by hunters and craftsmen. Not glamorous but they take a beating without complaint.
Gauntlets with copper-inlaid knuckles that warm slightly in combat. Popular with fighters who like a bit of theatre.
Thin gloves woven from enchanted thread. Casters find that spells initiated through them arrive just a fraction sooner.
Close-fitting leather gages favoured by mage-swordsmen. Cut to allow precise gestures without exposing the wrists.
Gauntlets of folded steel with a rune of endurance hammered into each palm. To wear them is to refuse to fall.
Practical cotton trousers with reinforced knees. Originally made for herders who spend long seasons in the field.
Loose-fitting slops with strapped cargo pockets on each thigh. Light enough to move fast, sturdy enough for rough terrain.
Cuisses of woven iron rings backed with thick felt. Standard melee armour for anyone past their first rank.
Wide-legged hakama tailored for fast pivoting and low stances. Said to have belonged to a dancer who killed like a soldier.
Cuisses stripped from a fallen warlord. The steel still bears the notches of an exceptional career.
Open sandals reinforced with hardened straps. Worn by travelling scholars who value comfort over appearance.
Greaves etched with the watch-sigils of a frontier garrison. Soldiers wore them into every border skirmish for a decade.
Articulated sollerets with exceptionally thin jointing. Allow a heavy fighter to move with surprising quickness.
Boots tipped with thornwood studs that grip loose stone and wet bark equally well. Near-silent underfoot.
Heavy iron sabatons bearing the crest of the graveward order. The last thing many opponents ever looked down at.

column13: A simple leather gorget with a brass fitting. Standard issue for range scouts and forward observers.
A thick iron-ringed choker worn by brawlers and heavy fighters who prefer neck protection they can feel.
A stiff academic collar lined with insulating ether-thread. Worn loose or tight depending on the wearer's disposition.
A finely linked chain bearing no adornment. Worn by fighters who believe skill speaks louder than decoration.
A solid iron torque inscribed with a warden's oath. Commanders award it only to soldiers who stood their ground absolutely.
A wide cowhide belt with a plain brass buckle. Unremarkable in every way. Gets the job done.
A cord of twisted ether-cloth bound in a simple knot. Mages use it to carry reagents but it quietly amplifies focus.
A wide linen sash worn tight across the abdomen. Used by mercenaries to support their core during long marches.
A formal obi woven with hexing patterns that contain and recycle magical overflow. Sought by serious elemental casters.
A girdle of overlapping iron plates said to have belonged to a Galka champion. Absurdly heavy. Absurdly effective.
A simple copper hoop earring. No enchantment to speak of, but the metal retains a small amount of protective warmth.
A small polished stone mounted on silver. Common gift between students completing their first year of magic study.
A heavy iron loop worn through the earlobe. Soldiers in some cultures earn the right to wear it after their first real battle.
A thin crystal stud that sharpens awareness when worn. Vendors argue endlessly over what mineral it actually is.
A feather-tipped earring crafted from the claw of a highland predator. Proof of a hunt that wasn't a sure thing.
A plain bronze ring with no markings. Picked up by adventurers because it costs nothing and weighs even less.
A ring given to new initiates at several academies. Enchanted faintly, enough to reassure a nervous student.
A steel ring stamped with a rank sigil. Many soldiers never take theirs off. Many graves have one on the finger.
A narrow platinum band inset with a dark stone. The stone grows warm the longer it is worn, which some find unsettling.
A broad iron ring engraved with a crossed-swords crest. Given to tournament champions. Most of those champions are gone.
A short cloak of rough undyed cloth. Keeps out wind and rain if nothing else. Very easy to replace.
A mottled mantle designed to break the wearer's silhouette in woodland. Also works surprisingly well in a crowd.
A short iron-banded cape worn at the garrison. Offers a little coverage to the back of the neck that armour plates miss.
A mantle stitched with ward-runes along every seam. Casters report that hostile spells occasionally fail to seat when wearing it.
A cloak that billows even in still air, as though caught in a private wind. Found on a nameless duelist at the end of a long road.

column15: FlavorText
A broad two-hander whose edge is pocked with rust that somehow never spreads. The weight alone does half the work.
A slim blade whose steel takes on a pale lustre at dusk. Favoured by battle mages who prefer their options open.
A narrow blade tapered to a vicious point. Cheap to make, easy to conceal, and surprisingly effective in the right hands.
A katana with a darkened blade that hides its movements in shadow. Said to whisper faintly when drawn from the scabbard.
A crude scythe fashioned from a salvaged blade and a long ashwood haft. Standard kit for a dark knight finding their footing.
A compact crossbow with a copper-inlaid lock mechanism that reduces misfires. Reliable over flashy.
A staff of ancient elderwood with a grain so tight it seems almost stone. Casters in remote regions prize it as a dependable tool.
Iron-reinforced knuckle guards with a textured grip that never slips. Simple, durable, and exactly as effective as they look.

column12: A plain iron visor riveted to a leather cap. Covers the essentials without any pretence of elegance.
A close-fitting hood woven from silk threaded with ether-conducting filaments. Keeps the caster's mind unnervingly still.
A wide-brimmed cap dyed in muted earth tones. Designed to keep the wearer unseen at the same time they are watching.
A full-coverage helm worn by frontier sentinels on extended postings. Heavy, unadorned, and built to last decades.
A training gi dyed in muddy earth tones with panels reinforced against repeated impact. Hard-wearing and comfortable.
A robe the colour of deep forest. Its fabric holds a faint charge that supplements the wearer's magical reserves.
A surcoat cut for freedom of movement, with hardened leather panels across the chest. Smells persistently of pine resin.
A coat of close-fitted tempered steel strips over a padded base. Favoured by career soldiers who value flexibility over bulk.
Thin cotton wraps reinforced at the knuckles with a stiffened inner layer. Worn to nothing and replaced often.
Close-fitting cuffs stitched with silver channelling thread along every seam. Marginally speeds the onset of spellcasting.
Gauntlets of overlapping iron vanes that protect without slowing the arm. Standard workshop output from a competent smithy.
Guards fashioned from laminated bone and thick hide. Heavier than they look and satisfyingly loud on contact.
Loose travelling kecks with deep pockets. Mages wear them for the mobility; scholars wear them because they have too many scrolls.
Kecks of interlocked bone plates over padded linen. Built for fighters who expect to be hit as often as they hit.
Slops woven at dawn from thread treated with early-morning dew. An affectation that somehow results in genuinely superior channelling.
Wide-legged breeches in a mottled pattern that is either camouflage or a laundry accident. Either way they do the job.
Sturdy leather boots with brass toecaps. Inelegant and effective. The mud never really comes off.
Thick-soled clogs with a surprisingly quiet footfall. Plodder is a nickname. The people who wear them are anything but.
Iron sabatons with an articulated veil of small plates across the instep. Allow a full range of motion without sacrificing coverage.

column13: A plain gorget stitched with a small white sigil. Healers starting out often trade one among themselves as a gesture of solidarity.
A braided cord hung with a single metal fang. Popular among fighters who prefer their accessories to carry a message.
A stiffened collar inscribed with concentric rings of notation. Scholars argue over whether the inscription is a formula or a poem.
A length of rough cord knotted at the waist. The enchantment on it is modest. The price is modest. Fair trade.
A belt hung with iron tassels that clatter when the wearer moves. Soldiers who know them find the sound reassuring.
A wide belt embroidered with binding sigils. Casters claim it keeps their concentration from fraying at the edges of long fights.
A small hooked earring worn by forward scouts. The enchantment is subtle enough that most opponents don't notice it working.
A teardrop stud of polished dark stone. The kind of earring a scholar wears to signal they have stopped trying to impress people.
A thick iron ring with a blunt surface finish. Worn by soldiers who want a ring that will survive the same things they do.
A narrow band set with two stones — one red, one blue. Said to represent the balance a true battlemage must maintain.
A short, dark cape cut to fall just below the shoulder blades. Worn by half the brigands on the continent and none of the merchants.
A healer's mantle embroidered with small white stitching along the hem. Given to field medics who have earned a bit of comfort.
A soldier's campaign cloak bearing no rank insignia. Whoever wore it served long enough that the markings simply wore away.

column15: FlavorText
A staff of elder-growth wood that has absorbed centuries of prayer. The grain runs upward. Healers say it already knows what they are about to cast.
A katana whose blade darkens entirely at the moment of the eclipse. Found sheathed in the chest of a shadow that refused to cast one.
A greataxe fashioned from ore extracted from the valley's deep ruin. It never needed sharpening. The edge was already there.

column12: Armour recovered from a Zilartian guardian whose allegiance was consumed by centuries of isolation. The metal is cold in a way that has nothing to do with temperature.

column11: Magic Damage Taken-8% / Shield Block Rate+5%
column12: Plate forged to honour a vow taken before a god that no longer answers. The inscription inside the collar reads only: hold.
A robe that hums with frequencies too low to hear but not to feel. Woven from materials that absorb light without re-emitting it.

column11: Reward HP Potency+15% / Pet TP Bonus+1000
column12: A cuirass of interlinked scales taken from a beast that had spent its life being the apex of things. It does not fit comfortably. Nothing that powerful does.
A helm of beaten silver fitted with a rangefinder lens. Belonged to a scout who was never tracked despite three decades of work in hostile territory.
Blood Pact Delay-10 / Avatar Perpetuation Cost-2
column13: A mantle stitched in patterns too complex to follow. Every avatar that has worn it grew stronger, then older, then was gone.
A torque of pale iron inscribed with musical notation that does not correspond to any known piece. Those who wear it hear an additional voice in every song.

column12: Sneak Attack DEX Bonus+5% / Triple Attack+1% / Waltz Potency+2%
column13: A ring inset with shadow-glass. The face of the last person who saw the previous owner wearing it is reportedly still visible in the stone.

column9: Spawns in the deeper grove section away from the main paths. ~1.5hr respawn.
column10: Absorbs Earth-based magic. Recommended: piercing damage and wind-element spells.
column11: An ancient treant warped by decades of dark energy pooling in the jungle floor. Bark armour and long reach. Patient.

column9: Patrols the upper section near the first banishing gate. ~1hr respawn.
column10: Fire-based weaponskills. Uses Souleater at 50% HP — healers should expect spike damage.
column11: A fire cultist who traded holy allegiance for pyroclast ambition. The plate he wears absorbed enough flame that it never fully cooled.

column9: Wanders the central plains. Rare spawn (~2hr). Does not aggro.
column10: High evasion. Uses melee WS chains rapidly. Kiting effective if solo. Ranged parties recommended.
column11: A ronin with no nation and no name left to use. Carries everything he owns. Has never lost a fight outdoors.

column9: Found in the upper beetle tunnel section. ~1hr respawn.
column10: AoE Counter-type ability activates when hit from the front. Engage from behind or use ranged.
column11: A monastery enforcer who outlived the order that trained him. Keeps discipline out of habit.

column9: Spawns in the lower mine shafts. Darkness required to navigate safely. ~1.5hr respawn.
column10: Drains HP on hit and uses dark-element spells. Dispel recommended. Light-based damage most effective.
column11: Something that used to be a miner. The scythe predates whatever it has become.

column9: Roams the northern coastal cliffs. ~1.5hr respawn.
column10: High Ranged Accuracy when enraged. Ice-based breath attack. Wind-element magic most effective.
column11: A highland predator that learned to hunt at range. The coldwood the beast favoured for scratching became the weapon.

column9: Spawns near the magical stone formations in the inner sanctuary. ~2hr respawn.
column10: Casts Tier III black magic and enfeebling spells. Silencing as priority. Does not have high HP but hits hard.
column11: A hexcaster who found the Zi'Tah's stones amplified her reach considerably. She never left.

column9: Patrols the lower prison corridors. ~1.5hr respawn.
column10: Generates high enmity and uses a self-Invincible-type ability at 30% HP. Do not burst — wait it out.
column11: A captain of a holy order disbanded by political decree. Still enforces laws no one else remembers.

column9: Found in the arcane chamber sections of the canal. ~1.5hr respawn.
column10: Casts Stoneskin and Phalanx repeatedly. Dispel before properly engaging. Uses Chainspell-type at 25% HP.
column11: A runeward arcanist who sealed himself into the canal's lower passages. He is still working on the same problem.

column9: Shares the dungeon with Ironvow Godefret — both farmable in the same run. Inner chamber. ~2hr.
column10: Self-cures aggressively and uses AoE knockback. Silence is mandatory. High MND makes enfeebles unreliable.
column11: A monastery elder who refused to leave when the institution fell. The passages became his sanctuary by default.

column9: Shares zone with Glacefang Velthar — farmable in the same excursion. Inner cape cliff section.
column10: Extremely high Ranged Accuracy and uses Eagle Eye Shot-type ability at 50% HP. Approach from downhill.
column11: A sharpshooter who operates entirely at range. Has never been caught in melee. Prefers it that way.

column9: Lurks in the wider tunnel chambers past the halfway point. ~2hr respawn.
column10: Very high physical defence — magic users or armour-penetrating WSs recommended. Slow but high ATK.
column11: A Gnole that reached warlord through the standard method: outlasting everyone who tried to stop it.

column9: Shares zone with Blight Serafi Yzen — farmable in same run. Outer sanctuary paths.
column10: High AGI and uses Ranged-type claw rush attacks. Silence ineffective — focus on kiting or stun rotation.
column11: The largest predator in the Zi'Tah. Its earring is actually one of its own teeth.

column9: Ambush-type NM — does not aggro but links with Tonberry trash. Inner temple. ~3hr respawn.
column10: High evasion. Uses Perfect Dodge once. Will attempt to kite and re-engage. Can be bound effectively.
column11: A master assassin who took a contract that led him into the temple. He's still working on the exit.

column9: Found in Den of Rancor mid-section. ~2hr respawn. Aggros by sight.
column10: Uses AoE Skillchain-type ability. Very high AGI and evasion. DEX-build parties outperform brute-force.
column11: A blade-dancer who treats combat as choreography. The choreography is lethal.

column9: Inner jungle paths near the Tonberry territory. ~2hr respawn.
column10: Calls a jug-pet-type add at pull. Defeat the pet first or it will be resumm oned. Add has moderate HP.
column11: A poacher lord who made the Yhoator his territory through persistence and strategic cruelty.

column9: Deep necropolis section. High-level undead trash. ~2.5hr respawn.
column10: Extremely high HP. AoE physical WS with wide range. Thunder-element magic and piercing damage recommended.
column11: A skeleton so old it has a name. What it was before is unclear. What it is now is very clear.

column9: Inner Feiyin sanctum. Shares zone with Iron-Knuckle Borvaag and The Nameless Blade — all three farmable per trip. ~2.5hr.
column10: Uses shield-type abilities and HP drain on hit. Light-based magic most effective. Keep distance.
column11: The ghost of a tournament champion who won everything and then lost the one fight that mattered.

column9: Deep Den of Rancor. Shares zone with Veilstep Manirak. ~3hr respawn.
column10: Uses Utsusemi and high-tier Ninjutsu. Bind/Gravity are effective. Rotate hate carefully — will punish backline.
column11: A shadow hunter who followed the darkness long enough that the darkness followed back.

column9: Upper grotto chambers above the serpent territory. ~2hr respawn.
column10: Dual-wields and casts enfeebles simultaneously. Resistant to Sleep. Dispel Stoneskin before engaging properly.
column11: A mage-swordsman who found the grotto's acoustics improved his casting. He stayed for the solitude.

column10: Calls two archer adds at 50% HP. Eliminate adds quickly — they apply a stacking ranged accuracy down.
column11: A frontier captain who refused evacuation orders. The tunnel is his post. It will remain so.

column9: Inner Feiyin sanctum. Shares zone with Bladeghost Arthek and The Nameless Blade. ~2.5hr.
column10: Massive HP pool. Uses Chakra repeatedly and has a high Counter rate. Blunt damage is absorbed — use slashing or piercing.
column11: A Galka champion who simply did not stop after death. Old habits.

column9: Inner sanctum. Shares zone with other Feiyin NMs. ~3hr respawn. Hardest NM in Feiyin.
column10: Uses multiple WSs per round below 30% HP. Extremely high evasion. AoE knockback on TP. Most dangerous of the Feiyin trio.
column11: No name on record. The cloak has been found three times on three different bodies in the same place.

column9: Mid-tower spawn between floors 4 and 6. ~2.5hr respawn.
column10: Uses Blue Magic abilities — toolkit varies. Silence is unreliable. Bring diverse debuff options.
column11: A faceless duelist who climbed the tower and never came back down. The visor is welded shut.

column9: Deep Den of Rancor. Shares zone with other Den NMs. ~3hr respawn.
column10: Uses Souleater-type drain strikes and high-STR WSs. Healers must pre-cure. Brings a single bodyguard add.
column11: A warlord who found the Den of Rancor and decided it suited him. It does.

column9: Deeper tomb section. Shares zone with Marrowlord Calagor. ~3hr respawn.
column10: Very high physical resistance — magic is the primary damage vector. Uses AoE holy-damage pulse at full HP.
column11: An armoured knight who was entombed standing. He has been standing ever since.

column9: Top floors of Delkfutt. Challenging trash on the approach. ~3hr respawn.
column10: Very high DEF and HP. Uses AoE Blind and Stoneskin. Thunder and fire magic recommended. Bring Dispel.
column11: A golem built to guard the tower's summit. No one specified when it should stop.

column9: Deeper grove section. Tough tree-based trash on approach. ~3hr respawn.
column10: Uses Souleater-type attacks and has extremely high base ATK. Healers are the priority target for hate rotation.
column11: The mark of a reaver: someone who cut a path through stronger opponents. Sorvath cut a long one.

column9: Central gardens. Access requires Zilart progression. Rare spawn (~4hr or forced via ???).
column10: Uses powerful physical WSs and AoE Void Pulse at 50% and 25% HP. Resistant to elemental magic. Requires coordinated hate rotation.
column11: A Zilartian guardian whose allegiance was consumed by isolation. Still holds its post. The post no longer exists.

column9: Central shrine chamber. Sky access required. ~4hr respawn.
column10: Very high DEF and HP. Casts Stoneskin and physical Barrier repeatedly. Thunder and fire magic best. Bring two Dispel sources.
column11: Forged to enforce a covenant between the Zilartians and something older. The covenant was forgotten. The golem was not.

column9: Sea-tier zone. Requires CoP progression. Hardest item to obtain in this set.
column10: Casts high-tier elemental magic and Dispels party buffs on TP. Resistant to enfeebles. Bring Magic Defense Bonus food.
column11: An arcanist consumed by the Emptiness without losing its spellcraft. It uses what remains to considerable effect.

column9: Inner temple sanctum. Spawns only during specific Lightsday windows. ~3hr window respawn.
column10: Cures itself and uses AoE light damage pulses. Dark magic is most effective. Do not engage on Lightsday — damage cap applies.
column11: A light-elemental spirit that has been resident in Ro'Maeve since before the temple had a name.

column9: Deepest Den of Rancor section. Hardest NM in the Den. ~4hr respawn.
column10: Uses Utsusemi and a Meikyo Shisui-type TP-flush. Attacks twice per round below 50% HP. Bind/Gravity effective early only.
column11: The most feared NM in the Den of Rancor. Has a name in three languages. None of them translate cleanly.

column9: Valley approach. Difficult path through high-level Gigas trash. ~3hr respawn.
column10: Massive HP. AoE Great Axe WS with wide radius. High base STR. Evasion strategies ineffective — stun rotation recommended.
column11: A Gigas warlord whose corruption made him stronger and considerably less interested in conversation.

column9: Outer garden perimeter. Sky access required. ~3hr respawn.
column10: Agile with high movement speed. Uses AoE Wing Blast at melee range — engage at ranged distance. Ranged parties recommended.
column11: An ancient aerial hunter bound to the gardens by the Zilartians. Still hunts. The gardens are smaller than it remembers.

column9: Outer temple wings. ~3hr respawn. Shares zone with Luminary Aethos.
column10: Summons a scaled avatar add at 70% HP — defeat it before re-engaging the NM. SMN counterstrategy recommended.
column11: An ancient summoner whose body is gone but whose contracts remain active. The avatars still answer.

column9: Upper necropolis section. Shares zone with Marrowlord Calagor and Gravewatch Ardan.
column10: Sings combat songs that simultaneously buff itself and debuff the party. Silence as priority. AoE Lullaby — spread party before each song cast.
column11: The ghost of a bard whose final performance was interrupted. It has been continuing ever since.

column9: Deep temple. Shares zone with Ebonveil Tachirak. Challenging Tonberry trash on approach. ~4hr.
column10: Uses Sneak Attack-type assassination and a stronger version of Tonberry's Grudge. Face NM away from party at all times.
column11: The Tonberry clan's champion. Unlike most Tonberries it is not patient. It has already decided what it is going to do.

column9: Far eastern boundary of the Zi'Tah. Shares zone with Razorfang Kellath and Blight Serafi Yzen.

column15: FlavorText
A plain blade with a leaf-pressed crossguard. Sold at every outpost. Dependable until something better turns up.
A slender duelling foil whose balance has been adjusted for spellcasting. The grip is wrapped in ash-threaded cord.
A broad sabre with a slightly green tint to the steel. Miners kept pulling it out of the same vein for years.
A blade that crackles faintly between strikes. The thunder effect is not decorative.
A heavy gladius with a darkened fuller. At lv18 the double attack proc is not subtle. It just hits again.
A ceremonial saber that turned out to be genuinely effective. Cure Potency on a sword is unusual. So is the person who earns this.
A two-handed claymore with a rough iron edge. Heavy for the level. Gets the job done by weight alone.
A great sword that returns something when it takes. DRK with Souleater active hit meaningfully harder with this in hand.
A two-hander that feels disproportionately punishing for lv20. Smite adds percent attack when wielding 2H. Players notice.
A short-handled hatchet with a thorn-pattern stamp on the blade. Good early axe. Nothing fancy.
A wide-bitted axe ground from red-tinged ore. Holds an edge well. Popular with BST who need reliable kit.
A heavy one-handed axe with a forward-weighted head. Zanshin gives follow-up swings on misses. At lv62 that matters.
An axe whose edge is notched in a way that suggests it hit something much harder than expected and kept going.
A broad-bladed greataxe with a wrapped grip. Reliable and appropriately heavy for the level. No tricks.
A tabar whose head still radiates heat. The fire add effect is consistent. The Smite bonus rewards 2H commitment.
A massive greataxe that a lv28 character has no business wielding efficiently. They do anyway.
A salvaged scythe with a pitted blade. DRK starting out will use this until something better appears. It takes a while.
A long-hafted scythe whose blade is stained in a way that does not come off. DRK find it aesthetically appropriate.
The last scythe. Drain and Aspir hitting 12% harder while this is equipped changes DRK sustain meaningfully.
A crude scythe that introduces DRK to Souleater Enhancement at lv22. First look at the mechanic. They remember it.
A polearm tipped with two diverging points. Split design was supposed to trap enemy weapons. Mostly it just stabs.
A spear with ember-treated tips that perform better against fire-resistant enemies. Practical in specific zones.
A DRG-exclusive bident. Jump ATT Bonus+15 directly boosts Jump and High Jump damage. Wyvern Breath enhancement is secondary.
A lance with a pronounced bore-tip. At lv24 Jump ATT Bonus+10 is the first time DRG feels like DRG.
A slim katana with a faint amber tint. Store TP+2 at lv24. It adds up.
A katana with petal engravings along the flat. Good mid-level option for NIN or SAM.
A NIN-exclusive katana. Tool Save+4% compounds per weapon if dual-wielded. DW+1 reduces off-hand penalty.
A pale katana that moves faster than it looks. Store TP+4 at lv18 is well ahead of anything in a casket.
A katana with fire-petal engravings. NIN-slanted due to the Ninjutsu skill bonus. SAM still benefits from TP and DEX.
A long tachi with an ivory-wrapped grip. Reliable SAM casket option. Store TP+4 builds toward weaponskill chains.
The SAM weapon. Store TP+6 with Zanshin follow-up and Skillchain Damage stacked. Chains happen faster and hit harder.
SAM's first meaningful great katana. Store TP+5 at lv30 with Skillchain Damage makes weaponskill chains feel intentional.
A plain iron mace carried by wandering healers. Healing Skill+3 at lv14 is genuinely useful.
A weighted cudgel used by enfeebling specialists. Solid Enfeeble Skill bonus makes debuffs land more reliably.
A tank healer's mace. Enmity+4 keeps cure threat manageable. Cure Potency+6% meaningfully extends MP efficiency.
The first time a lv18 WHM sees Cure Potency on a weapon. They do not put it away willingly.
A smooth wooden rod handed to new mages. MP+15 at lv16 is the whole point.
A staff laced with ore from a volcanic vein. Fire Affinity Damage boosts fire-element spell damage. Elemental Skill applies broadly.
BLM's priority Boss FATE staff. Magic Burst Bonus+8% is multiplicative on burst damage. Occult Acumen generates TP from nuke hits.
Magic Burst Bonus+5% at lv24 rewards parties that coordinate skillchains early. Uncommon to find this before lv30.
Broad-purpose mage stave. Conserve MP+3% compounds over a long fight. Healers and nukers both benefit.
